insight.title: How the light beneath our feet shapes your world
insight.subtitle: A quiet dance of glass and pulses connecting every moment

sections.text: Our world is held together by threads of glass. Beneath the concrete and under the salt of the deep ocean, billions of tiny light pulses race through hair-thin fibers. They carry every message you send and every memory you share. While the sky feels like the source of magic, the true power lives in the silent ground.

Instead of slow electricity, we use the speed of pure light. Think of it as a Morse code made of flashes, bouncing off the inside of glass tubes without ever escaping. This sequence of brightness creates the digital world. It is a tireless, luminous river flowing quietly through the dark earth.

This invisible net turns your morning routine into a global symphony. When you tap a screen, you aren’t just touching glass; you are reaching across continents in an eye-blink. Distance has become a choice rather than a barrier. We have replaced the physical weight of paper with the weightless speed of the sun.
We are no longer limited by where we stand, but by where we choose to look.

news.title: GIFT Nifty down 80 points; here's the trading setup for today's session
news.description: Markets concluded their sixth consecutive week of decline, falling by nearly half a percent amid heightened volatility. Analysts anticipate the upcoming week will remain data-intensive, with the US-Iran conflict and its impact on crude oil prices being critical market sentiment drivers. The Indian rupee surged over 2% on Thursday, marking its best single-day gain since 2013.
news.why: Prolonged market declines signal investor caution regarding major emerging economy growth.

news.title: Scientists find hidden brain cells helping deadly cancer grow
news.description: Scientists in Canada have uncovered a surprising weakness in glioblastoma, one of the deadliest brain cancers. They found that certain brain cells—once believed to only support healthy nerves—can actually help tumors grow by sending signals that strengthen cancer cells. When researchers blocked this communication, tumor growth slowed dramatically in lab models.
news.why: Understanding tumor mechanisms leads to more effective treatments for aggressive cancers.

news.title: Scientists identify trigger of Crohn’s scarring, research suggests
news.description: Researchers hope the findings could lead to the development of new treatments.
news.why: New research may lead to therapies preventing permanent intestinal damage in patients.

news.title: Steady Start Seen For Indonesia Stock Market
news.description: Ahead of the Good Friday holiday, the Indonesia stock market had turned lower again, one day after ending the four-day losing streak in which it had tumbled more than 240 points or 3.
news.why: Stable Southeast Asian markets reflect broader regional resilience amid global volatility.
